title: Sharp exponential rates for permanent-on-top and anomalous boson bunching at fixed rank
shortTitle: How fast permanent-on-top fails at fixed rank
oneLine: The sharp base is e/2 at complex rank two and e²/6 at real rank three; e^γ is a lower bound in general
abstract: The permanent-on-top conjecture of 1966 said that the permanent of a positive semidefinite matrix A is the largest eigenvalue of its Schur power Π(A), an n!-by-n! companion matrix that always has per A as one eigenvalue. Shchesnovich showed in 2016 that it is false; the question became by how much it can fail. The size of the failure bounds how badly a family of permanent inequalities can fail, enters the constants of permanent approximation (Anari, Gurvits, Oveis Gharan and Saberi), and limits anomalous bunching of partially distinguishable photons. This candidate proves that at every fixed rank d the worst ratio ‖Π(A)‖/per A grows exponentially in n with an exact base: e/2 ≈ 1.36 for complex rank two, e²/6 ≈ 1.23 for real rank three, with exact formulas for every d and both sequences rising to e^γ ≈ 1.78. The best general constant c* satisfies e^γ ≤ c* ≤ e^(1+γ) (previously only c* > 1 was known), and e^γ is the exact rate when the rank grows more slowly than √n. Balanced permanental compounds have the same bases, so an inequality of Pate fails exponentially. In the standard lossless optical model, two output ports with polarisation give exponential bunching enhancement with sharp base e/2, and the six standard polarisations give 62731/28800 ≈ 2.18 at twelve photons and more than 24,000 at sixty. Credit: the complex mixed–pure constant is Yuan and Parrilo's and the link uses the Christandl–König–Renner postselection technique. Limits: rates are asymptotic; whether c* = e^γ at full rank is open; optical numbers are model predictions with small absolute probabilities (about 3×10⁻⁵ at twelve photons). AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: A 14-page paper with a context-first introduction, written proofs of all theorems, limits, open problems and an AI-use statement. One Python program, code/verify_exp_rates.py, runs 28 checks: the constants g_C and g_R to 30 digits and their monotonicity, the bound of Theorem 1.2(a) on 36 random configurations, Shchesnovich's order-five example, the tetrahedral and octahedral closed forms against Ryser's formula, every quoted ratio and probability in exact rational arithmetic, and the incidence identity behind Theorem 5.1 (numpy 2.3.5, mpmath 1.3.0); every check raises an error on failure, even under python -O. These finite calculations test constants, closed forms and identities; they do not certify the asymptotic theorems. A clean replay in optimised mode reproduced the recorded results; changing the exact tetrahedral ratio 102469/74115 makes the program fail. Linux CI reruns the program and compares outputs exactly for exact fields and within declared tolerances (absolute 1e-12 or relative 1e-9) for floating-point fields.

keyResults: Theorem 1.1 (proof): for unit vectors in K^d (K = R or C) with d fixed, the worst ratio ‖Π(A)‖/per A grows like g_K(d)^n, with g_C(d) = e^{H_{d−1}}/d and g_R(d) = (2/d) exp{ψ(d/2) − ψ(1)}; thus g_C(2) = e/2 ≈ 1.36, g_R(3) = e²/6 ≈ 1.23, g_R(2) = 1, and both sequences increase strictly to e^γ ≈ 1.78.

Theorem 1.2 (proof): ‖Π(A)‖ ≤ C(n+d²−1, n) g_K(d)^n per A at rank at most d; the best general constant satisfies e^γ ≤ c* ≤ e^(1+γ) (lower bound new, upper bound Anari, Gurvits, Oveis Gharan and Saberi's); e^γ is the exact rate when the rank grows like o(√n).
Theorem 5.1 (proof): balanced permanental compounds have the same sharp bases, so Pate's 0/1 inequality fails with base e/2 at every complex rank d ≥ 2.

Corollary 6.1 (proof): the multimode bunching ratio of partially distinguishable photons has the same sharp bases; two output ports with polarisation give base e/2. Section 7: the six standard polarisations give exact model enhancements 62731/28800 ≈ 2.18 at twelve photons and more than 24,000 at sixty, with limit √(3/2) ≈ 1.22 per photon.

Credit and limits: the complex mixed–pure constant and its sharpness are Yuan and Parrilo's; the link uses the Christandl–König–Renner postselection technique. Rates are asymptotic; whether c* = e^γ at full rank is open; the optical values are predictions of the standard lossless model with small absolute probabilities (about 3×10⁻⁵ at twelve photons), not experiments.

decisionObject.description: Decide how far the permanent-on-top conjecture fails: the exact exponential rate of the worst ratio between the top Schur-power eigenvalue and the permanent at each fixed rank, the best general constant, and the consequences for permanental compounds and anomalous boson bunching.
decisionObject.scope: Positive semidefinite Gram matrices of unit vectors in R^d or C^d with d fixed and n growing; rank o(√n); balanced permanental compounds; the standard lossless model of partial distinguishability.
